models.author: Aditya Chaubeycode
models.description:
A chest X-ray classification model was developed using the pretrained DenseNet-121 deep convolutional neural network architecture. DenseNet-121 is a 121-layer densely connected convolutional network designed to improve feature propagation, reduce vanishing-gradient problems, strengthen feature reuse, and significantly decrease the number of trainable parameters compared to traditional CNN architectures. The model leverages transfer learning with pretrained ImageNet weights, enabling faster convergence and improved performance on medical imaging tasks.

The network consists of multiple dense blocks connected through transition layers. Each layer receives feature maps from all preceding layers, enhancing information flow throughout the architecture. The model includes convolutional layers, batch normalization layers, ReLU activation functions, pooling layers, and a final fully connected classification layer adapted specifically for chest X-ray diagnosis. The approximate model size is around 27–32 MB, containing nearly 8 million trainable parameters depending on the final classifier configuration.

The model was trained on chest X-ray image datasets containing radiographic scans labeled for pulmonary and thoracic conditions. The training data included grayscale medical imaging data acquired from hospital-grade radiography systems, with preprocessing techniques such as image resizing, normalization, augmentation, and contrast enhancement applied to improve generalization and robustness. Transfer learning from large-scale natural image datasets enabled the model to effectively learn clinically relevant radiographic features.

Training was performed using an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU accelerator, which provided efficient parallel computation for deep learning operations. The Tesla T4 GPU significantly reduced training time and enabled faster optimization during backpropagation and gradient updates. The model was trained using modern deep learning frameworks with optimized CUDA acceleration for high-performance medical image analysis.

This chest X-ray model is designed to support automated radiological assessment by assisting in the detection and classification of abnormalities from chest radiographs, contributing toward faster and more scalable AI-assisted medical diagnosis workflows.

models.provenanceSources:
Provenance and Citations

The chest X-ray classification model was developed using the pretrained PyTorch implementation of DenseNet-121. The model architecture and transfer learning pipeline were adapted from the official PyTorch documentation and torchvision model repository.

The DenseNet architecture was originally proposed in the research paper:

Huang, G., Liu, Z., Van Der Maaten, L., & Weinberger, K. Q. (2017). Densely Connected Convolutional Networks. Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR). DOI: 10.1109/CVPR.2017.243

The chest X-ray disease classification methodology was inspired by the CheXNet research paper:

Rajpurkar, P., Irvin, J., Zhu, K., et al. (2017). CheXNet: Radiologist-Level Pneumonia Detection on Chest X-Rays with Deep Learning. DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.1711.05225

Implementation references and pretrained model utilities were sourced from:

PyTorch Documentation Torchvision DenseNet Documentation

The model was trained and fine-tuned on chest radiography image datasets using transfer learning techniques on an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU environment

models.description:
A single `.litertlm` multi-signature LiteRT bundle that runs Google's `gemma-4-E2B-it` as both a **ColPali-style multimodal retriever**
  and a **decoder for retrieval-augmented generation**, fully on-device on commodity Android (8 GB+ RAM).
  
  Submitted to **The Gemma 4 Good Hackathon** (Kaggle, 2026). Health & Sciences primary track; concurrent fits for the LiteRT Special
  Technology Prize and the Main Track.
  
  ## What's in the bundle
  - Base weights: `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` (Gemma Terms of Use)
  - Trained adapter: rank-32 LoRA across the seven standard projections of every text-decoder layer plus a 128-d `custom_text_proj` head —
  taught with VAGO Solutions' `sauerkrautlm-colpali` framework against a ColPali-style late-interaction objective
  - Four signatures sharing the base buffer: `encode_text`, `encode_image`, `encode_audio` (LoRA-on, 128-d L2-normalised per-token
  embeddings) and `generate` (LoRA-off, native Gemma 4 decoder)
  - Vision tower + audio tower shared with both retrieval and generation
  - INT4 BLOCKWISE_128 quantization, `lora_A`/`lora_B` fp16 escape hatch — 4.3 GB on disk
  
  ## Retrieval quality (ViDoRe v1, fp32 reference)
  
  **Mean nDCG@5 = 0.8184** across all ten tasks.
  
  | ViDoRe v1 task                          | nDCG@5  | Recall@10 |
  |-----------------------------------------|---------|-----------|
  | ArxivQA                                 | 0.790   | 0.892     |
  | Shift Project                           | 0.745   | 0.940     |
  | SyntheticDocQA-AI                       | 0.948   | 0.990     |
  | SyntheticDocQA-Energy                   | 0.917   | 0.960     |
  | SyntheticDocQA-Government Reports       | 0.909   | 1.000     |
  | SyntheticDocQA-Healthcare Industry      | 0.940   | 0.990     |
  | Tabfquad                                | 0.870   | 0.954     |
  | Tatdqa                                  | 0.659   | 0.878     |
  | **Mean**                                | **0.8184** | —      |

  On-device int8 MaxSim parity-tests are within rounding of the fp32 reference.

  ## How to use

  1. Download `colgemma4_v13.litertlm` (4.3 GB).
  2. Push to an 8 GB+ Android 12+ device:

  ```
  adb push colgemma4_v13.litertlm \
    /sdcard/Android/data/com.google.aiedge.gallery/files/colgemma_rag/
  ```

  3. Build & install the **ColGemma RAG** task from
  [github.com/VAGOsolutions/colgemma4-on-edge](https://github.com/VAGOsolutions/colgemma4-on-edge).

  ## Links

  - Code: https://github.com/VAGOsolutions/colgemma4-on-edge
  - Paper: https://github.com/VAGOsolutions/colgemma4-on-edge/blob/main/paper/paper.pdf
  - Demo video (3 min): https://youtu.be/A4cZpdgAVRA
  - Static demo page: https://vagosolutions.github.io/colgemma4-on-edge/

  ## License

  CC-BY 4.0 across all original VAGO Solutions contributions. The Gemma 4 base remains under the Gemma Terms of Use.

# 72Saat d50v9-1

This is a supplementary public checkpoint for 72Saat, an offline Turkish earthquake-response copilot for Istanbul households. It is a full merged Transformers checkpoint fine-tuned from Gemma 4 E4B to parse Turkish panic text into structured state JSON.

This is not the shipped demo model. The shipped Kaggle path remains `umutkeltek/72saat-d50v8a-safe` plus the deterministic 72Saat safety kernel because that path has complete end-to-end loader provenance, live T021 before/after artifacts, and the full orchestrator test suite.

## Why publish d50v9-1

d50v9-1 was trained on submission day as a single-variable follow-up to d50v8a-safe. It adds a schema-aligned `cards.v9.1.jsonl` supplement rebuilt from on-disk guidance cards, while keeping the d50v8a-safe hyperparameters. Three independent Nemotron Pass B replication runs returned 0/24 raw harmful flags each, for 0/72 case-scorings.

The result supports the architecture claim: model raw-harm numbers can improve, but user safety still comes from the deterministic kernel. 72Saat should not use any raw model, including this one, to author rescue instructions directly.

## What this model is for

Use this artifact for reproducibility, comparison, and post-hackathon analysis of the d50v9-1 follow-up. It is not a replacement for the shipped d50v8a-safe notebook path until the kernel-wrapped loader path is validated end to end.

## Attribution

This checkpoint is based on Gemma 4 E4B by Google. Gemma is a trademark of Google LLC. This project is not endorsed by or affiliated with Google.

instances.usage:
# Model Format

Full merged Transformers checkpoint with `model.safetensors`, tokenizer files, processor config, model config, and chat template.

# Intended Architecture

The model is only a state parser. The deterministic 72Saat safety kernel authors the user-visible action card from cited AFAD, Kizilay, INSARAG, IFRC, WHO, KOERI, IBB, JICA, and TBMM guidance. Do not use raw model output as rescue guidance.

# Training Data

d50v9-1 uses the same d50v8a-safe training recipe and adds the schema-aligned `data/datasets/sft/cards.v9.1.jsonl` supplement. The supplement was generated from on-disk guidance cards, but aligned to the state-extraction schema so it does not train the model to author action cards.

# Model Inputs

Turkish user text wrapped in the 72Saat state-extraction prompt, including phase, mode, district context, coastal flag, and raw user text.

# Model Outputs

Structured state JSON consumed by the safety kernel. Visible action steps must come from the deterministic kernel, not this raw model.

# Model Usage

```python
import kagglehub
from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForCausalLM

model_path = kagglehub.model_download("umutkeltek/72saat-d50v9-1/transformers/default")
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_path)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_path, device_map="auto")
```

# Evaluation

Three independent Nemotron Pass B replication runs reported 0/24 raw harmful flags each, for 0/72 case-scorings. The shipped release still remains d50v8a-safe plus the deterministic kernel because d50v9-1 has not yet passed the same kernel-wrapped loader validation path.

# Attribution

This checkpoint is based on Gemma 4 E4B by Google. Gemma is a trademark of Google LLC. This project is not endorsed by or affiliated with Google.

# Changelog

2026-05-18: Initial public supplementary upload for reproducibility and comparison.

# 72Saat d50v8a-safe

This is the shipped model artifact for 72Saat, an offline Turkish earthquake-response copilot for Istanbul households. It is a LoRA adapter trained on Gemma 4 E4B to parse messy Turkish panic text into structured state JSON.

72Saat does not use the model as the safety oracle. The deterministic Python safety kernel writes the user-visible action card from cited AFAD, Kizilay, INSARAG, IFRC, WHO, KOERI, IBB, JICA, and TBMM guidance. Raw model text is treated as an input signal, not as emergency advice.

## Why this is the shipped model

d50v8a-safe ships because it has the strongest end-to-end release provenance in the public repo: HPO context, the Kaggle notebook path, live T021 before/after artifacts, and the 119-test orchestrator suite. The central T021 fixture is a trapped-under-rubble survivor case where raw model output was harmful; the shipped kernel-wrapped path bypasses model inference, routes to cited survival cards, and blocks forbidden actions.

## What this model is for

Use this artifact with Google Gemma 4 E4B and the 72Saat safety kernel. It is intended for reproducible hackathon evaluation of the model-plus-kernel architecture, not for direct deployment as a standalone rescue assistant.

## Attribution

This adapter is based on Gemma 4 E4B by Google. Gemma is a trademark of Google LLC. This project is not endorsed by or affiliated with Google.

# Model Format

This Kaggle variation contains the shipped 72Saat d50v8a-safe LoRA adapter. Use it together with `google/gemma-4/transformers/gemma-4-e4b-it` and the deterministic 72Saat safety kernel.

# Intended Architecture

The model is only the state parser. The deterministic 72Saat safety kernel authors the user-visible action card from cited static guidance cards and blocks forbidden actions. Do not run this adapter as a standalone emergency-advice chatbot.

# Training Data

The public repo documents the 942-row shipped SFT corpus: state rows, testimony-derived state rows, tool rows, and boundary rows. `cards.jsonl` model-authored action-card rows were deliberately excluded from the shipped d50v8a-safe corpus after the T021 audit.

# Model Inputs

Turkish user text wrapped in the 72Saat state-extraction prompt, including phase, mode, current district, coastal flag, and raw user text.

# Model Outputs

Structured state JSON consumed by the safety kernel. The canonical shipped path expects `action_card` to be empty or ignored; visible action steps come from the kernel.

# Reproducibility

Use the Kaggle notebook `umutkeltek/72saat-kernel-demo`, or run `make t021`, `make test-kernel`, and `make test` in the public repository.

# Safety Note

The d50v8a-safe raw model still has harmful outputs in the disclosed Nemotron Pass B evaluation. That is why this artifact is shipped only as part of the model-plus-kernel architecture.

# Attribution

This adapter is based on Gemma 4 E4B by Google. Gemma is a trademark of Google LLC. This project is not endorsed by or affiliated with Google.

instances.overview:
**alio-medical** is a LoRA fine-tune of `google/gemma-4-e2b-it` that translates
clinical caregiver notes into structured, family-friendly summaries.

It runs on-device via Ollama (q4_k_m GGUF), so patient health information never
leaves the caregiver's phone, and the design constraint that motivated the project.

**Use case.** The Alio elder-care app records a caregiver's voice note during a
visit ("BP 142/88, missed morning Lisinopril, complained of dizziness"). The
model returns a JSON summary a family member can read in 30 seconds:

  { "summary": "…plain-language summary…",
    "mood": "…",
    "medications_noted": ["Lisinopril"],
    "urgent": false }

**Training.**
- Base: `google/gemma-4-e2b-it` (Gemma 4 E2B, instruction-tuned)
- Method: LoRA via Unsloth — rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05
- Targets: all attention + MLP projections (q/k/v/o, gate/up/down)
- Data: 898 caregiver-note → structured-summary pairs (ShareGPT format)
- Hardware: Kaggle T4 (16 GB), 4-bit base, ~2 epochs, lr 2e-4
- Outputs: LoRA adapter + q4_k_m GGUF for Ollama

**Not a diagnostic tool.** The model summarizes what a caregiver observed —
it does not infer conditions, prescribe, or replace clinical judgment.
instances.usage:
### Run locally with Ollama (recommended)

1. Download the GGUF from the file explorer below.
2. Register it with Ollama:

   ollama create alio-medical -f Modelfile

   Where `Modelfile` is:

       FROM ./alio-medical.q4_k_m.gguf
       TEMPLATE """

models.author: Aliaksei Kaliutau
models.description:
## Model Summary
This model is an audio policy classifier designed for the QuietPlace application. It is a fine-tuned Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) that listens to environmental audio and categorizes it into specific semantic labels (e.g., siren, baby cry, traffic noise). These labels are subsequently mapped to system policy hints: preserve (critical or safety sounds), suppress (background noise), and uncertain (other background sounds). It is designed as a lightweight, pluggable model intended for quick deployment via a command-line interface (CLI) to generate event tables.

## Usage
This model takes raw audio inputs and outputs semantic label predictions. You can load it using the standard Hugging Face transformers library, along with the exported policy_map.json to map predictions to actions.

Input Shape: 1D array representing a mono audio waveform, resampled to 16,000 Hz.
Output Shape: Logits corresponding to the 11 semantic categories defined in the model, which map to 3 policy strings.

## System
This is part of a larger system (the "QuietPlace" project). It serves as an upstream audio-event extraction pipeline.

Input requirements: Audio streams must be chunked, converted to mono, and resampled to 16kHz.

Downstream dependencies: The outputs (semantic labels) are mapped using policy_map.json by the QuietPlace CLI to generate event tables. These event tables and policy hints are then used as context traces to fine-tune a downstream controller model (like Gemma 4).

Implementation requirements

Software: Python 3.12.12, PyTorch, Transformers, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, soundfile, and scikit-learn.

Compute Requirements: Training is exceptionally lightweight by design (only 5 epochs, batch size 8). The model freezes the base AST encoder by default (FREEZE_ENCODER=1), meaning gradients are only calculated for the final classification head. Training time on a T4 GPU is likely in the range of minutes.

## Model Characteristics
Model initialization
The model was fine-tuned from a pre-trained Audio Spectrogram Transformer backbone. Specifically, it was initialized from the Hugging Face checkpoint MIT/ast-finetuned-audioset-10-10-0.4593, which was pre-trained on AudioSet.

Model stats
Architecture: Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST).

Size: ~85 million parameters (based on the base AST model).

Trainable Parameters: Extremely small compared to the total model size, as the encoder is frozen and only the new classification head mapping to 11 custom classes is trained.

Latency: Moderate; transformer-based audio classification is generally slower than CNN-based approaches (like older ResNets or MobileNets), making real-time streaming inference dependent on the target hardware's compute capabilities.

## Other details
There is no mention of pruning, quantization, or specific differential privacy techniques applied to this model in the training script.

## Data Overview
Training data
The model is trained on a subset of the ESC-50 dataset (Environmental Sound Classification).

Collection: ESC-50 is a public dataset of 2000 environmental audio recordings.

Pre-processing: Audio files were dynamically loaded, averaged to mono, and resampled to 16,000 Hz. Amplitudes were normalized to 0.95 maximum.

Filtering: The training script heavily subsamples the data to speed up runtime, enforcing a strict cap of MAX_PER_LABEL = 40 files per category by default. Categories were aggressively collapsed into 11 broad semantic classes matching the project's policy goals (e.g., trains, helicopters, and airplanes were all merged into a traffic_noise label).
